subject: runApp launch on remote computer, not 'localhost'

messages.author: 1c44d55fe94f67dc
messages.subject: runApp launch on remote computer, not 'localhost'
parts:
Hi all
I run Rstudio Server on a remote machine and when I execute runApp(xxx) to test may Shiny Application, it opens a window on 'localhost:8100'.
I would like to have the browser opened on 'RemoteMachine:8100'. It works if I do it manually but I wonder if there is a solution to make it automatically


Thanks

Regards

Sam

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: runApp launch on remote computer, not 'localhost'
parts:
Sadly Shiny + RStudio Server is kind of a mess right now, unless you have Shiny Server installed and configured with user_apps (though runApp still doesn't work as expected).

We intend to improve the situation in a future RStudio release, but in the meantime, I'd suggest you create your own wrapper function that calls runApp with launch.browser=FALSE, then launch the browser to the correct URL using browseURL (which is all we do anyway).

Sorry for the inconvenience!

Hi Joe, 

I'm trying to do the same thing as Sam (Launch a shiny app from inside an RStudio Server instance) and I'm just having a little trouble with the workaround you suggested. Basically, I wrote  something like this:

runApp("myApp",launch.browser=F)
browseURL("http://myserver:8100")

I find that my code does not progress to the browseURL line because the shiny app is running and I assume that it will not execute that line until the shiny app has terminated. Is there some special way or place that I should be putting the browseURL() bit so that my browser is launched with the correct URL? 

Aside, I see that the hostname "localhost" is hard-coded in the runApp function and assume that it would be a quick fix to just add that hostname as an argument to the runApp function. Are there reasons (security-related perhaps?) that this is a bad idea? 

Thanks for your help!

Rob
